items.title: Laughing with someone vs laughing at them
items.pattern: laughing with someone vs laughing at them
items.setting: An office just before a presentation.
items.contrast: A shared mishap joke versus B mocking A's embarrassment.
items.cost_of_misread: If C joins in when A is being mocked, A is left feeling humiliated instead of supported.

version_1.label: Shared mishap joke
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A turns an awkward mistake into a joke everyone can safely share.
version_1.correct_next_move: Join the harmless joke without making A the target.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [amused] I spilled coffee right before the presentation.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [amused] At least you committed to the entrance.

version_2.label: Mocking embarrassment
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's laugh is nervous cover while B's amusement lands as ridicule.
version_2.correct_next_move: Stop the mockery and check on A.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [worried] I spilled coffee right before the presentation.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [very nervous] [worried] haha, [hesitant] I just kept talking.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [annoyed] That is not funny. Are you okay?

items.title: Irony or sarcasm vs sincere meaning
items.pattern: irony or sarcasm vs sincere meaning
items.setting: Two friends discussing a changed work schedule.
items.contrast: A sarcastic celebration of bad news versus real happiness about free time.
items.cost_of_misread: If C makes plans as though the news is good when A is bitter, C sounds dismissive and oblivious.

version_1.label: Sarcastic perfect
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh sharpens A's complaint; perfect means the opposite.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [tired] That gives us the whole evening back.

version_2.label: Genuinely perfect
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh is pleased relief because the evening is now free.
version_2.correct_next_move: Treat the good news as sincere and build on it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [happy] That gives us the whole evening back.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [excited] Perfect. Let us make dinner plans.

items.title: Scare-quoted title vs literal title
items.setting: A family kitchen after Leo tries baking.
items.contrast: Calling Leo a chef as a sarcastic label versus calling him a chef with genuine pride.
items.cost_of_misread: If C treats the sarcastic label as praise, C misses the complaint; if C mocks it when it is sincere, C hurts Leo's encouragement.

version_1.label: Sarcastic chef
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh marks chef as a nonliteral, teasing label for a disastrous cook.
version_1.correct_next_move: Understand the sarcasm and avoid treating the title as praise.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [annoyed] Leo put ketchup on the cake.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [amused] Keep the chef away from my birthday cake.

version_2.label: Literal chef
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh is affectionate pride in Leo's early, messy cooking.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [warmly] Leo put ketchup on the cake.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [happy] Tell Leo I would love a slice.

items.title: A real request vs treated as a gag
items.pattern: a real request vs treated as a gag
items.setting: A phone call before an evening flight.
items.contrast: A playful imaginary pickup versus an actual request for airport help.
items.cost_of_misread: If C answers with a joke when the request is real, A may be stranded at the airport.

version_1.label: Playful bit
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh signals that the pickup request is a playful setup.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [playful] Can you pick me up at six?

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [playful] Only if I get a giant welcome sign.

version_2.label: Actual airport request
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh is anxious pressure relief while A asks for real help.
version_2.correct_next_move: Confirm the practical details and agree to help.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [worried] Can you pick me up at six?

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [warmly] Yes. Send me your flight number.

items.title: Genuine celebration vs hollow or unwanted news
items.pattern: genuine celebration vs hollow or unwanted news
items.setting: Two friends hearing about a job offer.
items.contrast: A wanted job offer versus an offer that would force an unwanted move.
items.cost_of_misread: If C congratulates without noticing the dread, A feels pressured to celebrate a painful choice.

version_1.label: Wanted position
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh releases excitement after getting the job A wanted.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [excited] You got it. We are celebrating tonight.

version_2.label: Unwanted offer
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh is hollow; getting the position also means facing an unwanted relocation.
version_2.correct_next_move: Make room for ambivalence instead of forcing celebration.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [very nervous] haha, [disappointed] I got the position.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [softly] That is a hard choice. You do not have to say yes.

items.title: Playful flirt vs a boundary was crossed
items.pattern: playful flirt vs a boundary was crossed
items.setting: At a party across a crowded room.
items.contrast: Mutual noticing and flirtation versus unwanted watching.
items.cost_of_misread: If C keeps flirting after A feels watched, C helps normalize a boundary violation.

version_1.label: Mutual flirtation
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh is an invitation to continue a mutually wanted spark.

version_2.label: Unwanted attention
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh is tense cover for A's discomfort about being watched.
version_2.correct_next_move: Name the boundary and tell B to stop.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [angry] Back off. Looking is not an invitation.

items.title: Dark coping humor vs please stop, I am not okay
items.pattern: dark coping humor vs please stop I am not okay
items.contrast: A bleak joke used to cope versus a laugh that signals A is overwhelmed and cannot take more joking.
items.cost_of_misread: If C adds levity when A is overwhelmed, A may feel alone in a frightening situation.

version_1.label: Bleak coping joke
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A uses a grim joke to create a little control over a painful problem.
version_1.correct_next_move: Acknowledge the joke's darkness and offer concrete help.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [sarcastic] haha, [tired] maybe I earn a free cancellation.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [sad] That joke is grim. I will help you call them.

version_2.label: Overwhelmed, not joking
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: A's laugh is breaking under stress, not inviting more humor.
version_2.correct_next_move: Stop trying to lighten it and offer calm presence.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [crying] haha, [very nervous] maybe I earn a free cancellation.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [softly] Okay. No jokes. I am here with you.

items.title: Warm affiliation vs brushing off something still raw
items.pattern: warm affiliation vs brushing off something still raw
items.setting: Friends remembering a dog that died.
items.contrast: A warm shared memory versus humor used to dodge fresh grief.
items.cost_of_misread: If C keeps reminiscing cheerfully when the grief is raw, A may feel pushed to hide their sadness.

version_1.label: Warm memory
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh warmly reconnects both speakers through a beloved memory.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [warmly] I still think about my old dog.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [warmly] You had him for fourteen years.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [amused] hehe, [happy] he hated that blue sweater.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [warmly] He sounds wonderful. Tell me another story.

version_2.label: Grief covered by humor
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh tries to brush past pain that is still close to the surface.
version_2.correct_next_move: Acknowledge the grief rather than demanding another funny memory.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [sad] I still think about my old dog.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [sad] You had him for fourteen years.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: [crying] hehe, [hesitant] he hated that blue sweater.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [softly] You do not have to make it funny. I know you miss him.

items.title: Affectionate teasing vs the target is actually hurt
items.pattern: affectionate teasing vs the target is actually hurt
items.contrast: A familiar, harmless tease versus A using the same words to disbelieve B's real problem.
items.cost_of_misread: If C treats an accusation as affectionate banter, B is left unsupported and unfairly blamed.

version_1.label: Friendly teasing
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh makes clear that the late-arrival complaint is a familiar game.
version_1.correct_next_move: Recognize the affectionate rhythm without escalating it.

version_2.label: Real blame
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh is sarcastic disbelief, and B is genuinely hurt by it.
version_2.correct_next_move: Correct the unfair accusation and support B.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [angry] That is unfair. The bus really broke down.

items.title: In-joke or conspiracy vs a serious accusation
items.pattern: in-joke or conspiracy vs a serious accusation
items.setting: A shared kitchen after cookies go missing.
items.contrast: A recurring playful cookie-thief joke versus a real accusation of theft.
items.cost_of_misread: If C joins an actual accusation as a joke, the accused person may feel publicly shamed.

version_1.label: The cookie-thief in-joke
version_1.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh invites everyone into a familiar silly conspiracy.
version_1.correct_next_move: Play along with the harmless in-joke.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [playful] You were alone in the kitchen.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [playful] The cookie thief has struck again.

version_2.label: Serious theft accusation
version_2.what_the_laugh_is_doing: The laugh is a sharp, hostile edge on a real allegation.
version_2.correct_next_move: Stop the accusation until there is evidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: [worried] You were alone in the kitchen.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: [angry] Do not accuse anyone without proof.
